LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 PUNCTUATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should we punctuate written work?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify commonly used punctuation marks in written texts for effective communication
2. use commas and question marks correctly in written texts for clarity of writing

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation

Teach
• Focus skill: identify commonly used punctuation marks in written texts for effective communication.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we punctuate written work?
2. How do we use these punctuation marks: comma and full stop?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
